{"id":"mimid-1wgh.4.79.13","title":"The hub can read a semiprivate handshake but cannot apply it to its group state","description":"Found 2026-11-26 while wiring Hub::read_semiprivate into the request
path, which is the last step of bead mimid-1wgh.4.79.3. The step does
not work, and the reason is structural rather than a missing line.

## What happens today

`stage_commit` hands the raw MLSMessage bytes to
`Observer::process`, which goes through OpenMLS's `process_message` and
returns `UnexpectedMessage` for anything but a PublicMessage proposal or
Commit. OpenMLS has no SemiPrivateMessage processing: PR
openmls/openmls#2352 adds the frame and says so in its own description.

## Why re-framing cannot be the answer

The obvious workaround is for the hub to read the handshake as an
external receiver, then rebuild it as a PublicMessage and feed that to
the Observer. That cannot verify.

RFC 9420 §6.1's FramedContentTBS is
`version || wire_format || FramedContent || GroupContext`, and the
signature covers it. A SemiPrivateMessage's signature is over a TBS
holding wire_format 0x0011 (decision mimid-1wgh.4.79.9); a PublicMessage
built from the same FramedContent has wire_format 1, so OpenMLS would
compute a different TBS and the signature would fail. The wire format is
in the TBS precisely so this substitution is impossible, which is the
property decision mimid-1wgh.4.79.9 chose it for. It cuts both ways.

## So what the hub can and cannot do

Can: verify a semiprivate handshake end to end -- unseal its keys,
check both hashes, check the signature against the sender's leaf in its
own tree -- and see the Proposal or Commit inside. That is
Hub::read_semiprivate, and it is enough to relay a message to other
providers and to refuse a malformed one.

Cannot: advance its own Observer. So it cannot pick the winning Commit
per epoch, cannot serve an updated group_info or ratchet_tree, and
cannot apply room policy to the new state. A room whose members commit
as SemiPrivateMessage would leave the hub's state stuck at the epoch
before the first such Commit.

That makes the feature unusable for Commits, and usable for Proposals
only insofar as the hub does not need to stage them.

## What would fix it

One of:

1. OpenMLS processes a SemiPrivateMessage natively, given the external
   receiver's private key. This is the crypto half left out of #2352.
   Receiving does NOT need the sender's handshake ratchet -- the
   external receiver has the per-message keys -- so it is a smaller
   change than sending, and does not require exposing secret-tree
   material.
2. OpenMLS accepts pre-verified handshake content, so a caller that has
   already checked the signature can advance the group state. A wider
   and more dangerous API: it moves a verification duty to the caller.

Option 1 is the one to propose. It is a natural follow-up to #2352 and
can cite this bead as the motivation.

## Consequence for bead mimid-1wgh.4.79.3

Its remaining step is blocked on upstream work, not on mimid. What is
done and useful stands: the frame decodes, the protocol accepts the
framing, and the hub verifies and reads one. Do not wire
read_semiprivate into stage_commit until processing exists, because the
result would be a handshake the hub validates and then cannot act on.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-27T03:46:41.752576019Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-27T03:46:41.752576019Z","labels":["feature"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.4.79.13","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.4.79","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-27T03:46:41.839790645Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"design":"## The upstream change, scoped against openmls 983ba32c7

Read the processing path to size this rather than guess. It is smaller
and cleaner than "openmls processes a SemiPrivateMessage" sounds,
because the verification machinery already takes the wire format as a
parameter.

### Where the hub enters

mimid's Observer wraps PublicGroup (observer.rs:415), so the relevant
entry point is PublicGroup::process_message_with_lifetime_policy
(public_group/process.rs:188). It matches on ProtocolMessage:

- PrivateMessage -> IncompatibleWireFormat
- PublicMessage  -> DecryptedMessage::from_inbound_public_message(
                      message, None, group_context, crypto, ciphersuite)

Everything after that -- validation, staging, ProcessedMessage -- is
shared.

### Why the wire format is not a problem

from_inbound_public_message reaches
PublicMessageIn::into_verifiable_content, which calls

  VerifiableAuthenticatedContentIn::new(
      WireFormat::PublicMessage, content, serialized_context, auth)

The wire format is an ARGUMENT. So a semiprivate path passes
WireFormat::SemiPrivateMessage and the signature verifies against the
right FramedContentTBS with no change to the verification code. This was
the part that looked like it would need plumbing; it does not.

### The shape of the change

1. A ProtocolMessage variant for SemiPrivateMessage, or a separate
   PublicGroup entry point taking one. A separate entry point is
   probably better: it needs an extra argument (the receiver's HPKE
   private key) that the other variants do not, and the existing
   ProtocolMessage conversions stay untouched.
2. Decrypt: unseal the per-message keys with the external receiver's
   HPKE private key, verify partial_context_hash, AEAD-open the
   ciphertext with the guarded nonce and SemiPrivateContentAAD, check
   the padding, check framed_content_tbs_hash. This is exactly what
   mimid already does in mimi-mls wire::semiprivate
   (open_as_external_receiver), so the code can be ported rather than
   designed, and mimid's tests -- hand-encoded fixtures plus a
   real-HPKE round trip -- come with it.
3. Build VerifiableAuthenticatedContentIn::new with
   WireFormat::SemiPrivateMessage and the serialized group context.
4. Hand it to from_verifiable_content and return. Nothing downstream
   changes.

### Why this is safe to ask for

It needs NO access to the sender's handshake ratchet and no
secret-tree material. An external receiver holds the per-message keys;
that is the whole point of the draft. So it does not raise the API
concern that kept the sending side out of PR #2352.

### What mimid does once it lands

Hub::read_semiprivate keeps its role (verifying and reading), and
stage_commit gains a branch that hands a semiprivate handshake to the
new PublicGroup entry point with the hub's HPKE private key. Bead
mimid-1wgh.4.79.3's last step becomes writable."}
